day.day_focus: Luke 15:1-2 - All the tax collectors and the sinners were coming near Him to listen to Him

scripture.text: Now all the tax collectors and the sinners were coming near Him to listen to Him. Both the Pharisees and the scribes began to grumble, saying, “This man receives sinners and eats with them.”

exposition.text: Luke 15:1-2 opens with a scene marked by resurrection mercy in community life. The text turns mercy into visible resurrection-shaped hope before a watching community. The passage puts one clear scene in front of us: All the tax collectors and the sinners were coming near Him to listen to Him. We should stay with that scene before we rush to a slogan. Because this is narrative material, the theology arrives through events, actions, and speech rather than detached maxims. That keeps the reading honest. The wider context matters too. Luke 15:1-2 belongs to a larger movement in which Jesus is being received, resisted, watched, and answered. So the burden here is resurrection mercy in community life. The theological lane is resurrection mercy that strengthens communal witness. The passage stays concrete through Now all the tax collectors and all, tax, collectors. Resurrection mercy strengthens communal witness by turning compassion into visible hope before many observers. What we see in Luke 15:1-2 shows how people respond when Jesus stands near and the cost of discipleship is no longer theoretical. The point is not bare information. It presses into resurrection mercy instead of detached admiration of power. We should not drift into generic encouragement detached from the scene. We should let the passage name the pressure point for the day. If the scene is shaped by All the tax collectors and the sinners were coming near Him to listen to Him, then obedience today should answer that same pressure point. Where the text exposes fear, we should practice mercy that strengthens communal witness to the risen Christ. Where it honors devotion, we should practice acts of mercy that strengthen resurrection-shaped witness in community. Where it reveals Jesus clearly, we should pursue mercy that makes resurrection hope tangible in community life rather than delay. That keeps the day under the authority of Scripture. Strong exposition stays close to the text. It does not chase a clever slogan. It lets the details do their work on the conscience. That kind of reading slows us down. It teaches us to listen before we react. It also keeps prayer and application from drifting away from the passage. The passage sustains courage because Jesus remains worthy of trust in costly moments. The church's witness is strengthened when daily conduct aligns with confessed doctrine. Community-resurrection passages show that mercy and resurrection hope become public encouragement for many, not just private consolation for one. They therefore should move toward communal witness rather than isolated amazement. prompts: Sit with Luke 15:1-2 for two quiet minutes. Read the scene of resurrection mercy in community life slowly and let it settle before you move on.
Where does this passage call for acts of mercy that strengthen resurrection-shaped witness in community today?
Stay for one more minute and answer God with one honest sentence of trust, repentance, or gratitude before continuing.

items: Name one place where you have been trying to control the outcome, and entrust that concern to God in prayer.
End the day by recording one evidence of God's goodness you noticed in work, rest, or relationships.
action_steps.connector_phrase: Because Luke 15:1-2 calls for acts of mercy that strengthen resurrection-shaped witness in community today:

prayer.text: Father, thank You for speaking clearly in Luke 15:1-2. In this passage You bring resurrection mercy in community life into the open through All the tax collectors and the sinners were coming near Him to listen to Him. Lord Jesus, keep us from reading these words as distant history only, and press them into our ordinary obedience today. Where we resist the truth highlighted in this reflection, bring repentance and renewed trust. Keep us near Your word, and do not let ordinary pressure turn us away from humble obedience. Holy Spirit, take what we have seen in the exposition and turn it into worship instead of mere information. Teach us to remember that Luke 15:1-2 opens with a scene marked by resurrection mercy in community life. Guard our speech from haste, our work from pride, and our choices from whatever would pull us away from resurrection mercy instead of detached admiration of power. Help us practice the obedience this day requires with humility as we pursue acts of mercy that strengthen resurrection-shaped witness in community. Amen.
